property_summary: For any caller and any ETH amount, calling Deposit increases that caller's balances entry by exactly msg.value in the reference; the mutant fails because it leaves balances unchanged for some deposits.

For any caller and any nonzero deposit amount, after calling Deposit the reference contract increases that caller's balances by the sent msg.value; the mutant fails because Deposit does not add msg.value and therefore leaves balances unchanged for some deposits.

For every caller and deposit amount, after calling Deposit the contract's balances for that caller is at least the sent msg.value greater than its prior value (i.e., balances[caller]_after >= balances[caller]_before + msg.value); the mutant that omits adding msg.value can violate this (balances unchanged).

For any depositor and amount, after calling Deposit the reference contract's balances at the depositor's address strictly increases by the deposited msg.value compared to its prior value; the mutant that assigns balances[msg.sender] = balances[msg.sender] (forgetting to add msg.value) violates this for some deposit inputs.

For any depositor and deposit amount, after calling Deposit the total sum of all individual balances (sum over addresses seen in History) increases by msg.value in the reference, but the mutant can leave balances unchanged so the total tracked sum does not increase for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonnegative msg.value, Deposit never decreases any account's recorded balance (balances[key] after Deposit is >= balances[key] before); the mutant subtracts msg.value and can decrease balances, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonnegative deposit value, calling Deposit never decreases any account's recorded balance (every balances[k] after Deposit is >= before); the mutant subtracts msg.value and can make some balances[k] smaller, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any depositor and any deposit value, calling Deposit never decreases that depositor's recorded balance (balances[msg.sender] after Deposit >= balances[msg.sender] before); the mutant subtracts msg.value from the caller's balance and can make it smaller, violating this rule for some inputs.

For any caller, any deposit value, and any observed key k, calling Deposit never decreases balances(k) in the correct contract (balances(k)_after >= balances(k)_before); the mutant subtracts msg.value on Deposit and can make some balances(k) smaller, violating this invariant for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor, depositing a positive amount increases the depositor's recorded balance by exactly the deposited amount (balances[msg.sender]_after == balances[msg.sender]_before + msg.value); the mutant subtracts msg.value and so violates this for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, calling Deposit increases that caller's stored balance by exactly the deposited amount (i.e., balances[caller] after Deposit == balances[caller] before + msg.value); the mutant overwrites instead, so for some inputs this equality is broken.

For any caller and deposit amount, after Deposit the caller's stored balance equals its previous balance plus msg.value; the mutant assigns msg.value instead, so for callers with pre-existing nonzero balances this equality can be violated.

For any depositor and deposit amount, if some other address k had a nonzero prior balance, then after the depositor calls Deposit the other address k's balance is unchanged in the reference but the mutant can overwrite balances for arbitrary keys, so there exists inputs where balances(k) differs between reference and mutant.

For any depositor addr and any key k, after calling Deposit() the reference contract preserves other keys' balances (balances(k) unchanged) while the mutant can overwrite balances[k] with msg.value, so there exist addr,k,amount where balances(k) differs between reference and mutant.

For any depositor and any key k, calling Deposit() preserves the balance of every other address k (i.e. balances(k) does not change) — the mutant wrongly assigns balances[msg.sender] = msg.value which can overwrite balances for other keys if storage collision or attacker manipulates msg.sender via a contract, breaking the preservation.

For any caller and any positive msg.value, a single Deposit call increases that caller's balances by exactly msg.value; the mutant that adds a second increment can make the balance increase by 2*msg.value and thus violate this equality for some inputs.

For any caller and any deposit value, a single Deposit call increases that caller's recorded balance by exactly the sent msg.value; the mutant that double-increments balances can make the increase equal 2*msg.value, violating this equality for some fuzzed inputs.

For any depositor address A and any nonzero deposit v, after calling Deposit() once from A with value v, the contract's balances(A) increases by a value that is equal to the previous balance plus the total contract ETH balance increase (i.e. balances increase equals address(c).balance increase); the mutant double-increments balances making balances diverge from the contract's actual ether held and thus break this invariant for some inputs.

For any sequence where an address A makes two deposits of values v1 and v2 (non-negative), the net change in C.balances(A) equals v1+v2; the mutant that double-adds on each Deposit can make the recorded balance exceed the actual sum of deposited amounts for some fuzzed v1,v2 and caller, so the property is violated.

For any depositor address A and any non-negative deposit value v, if A calls Deposit() with value v while the contract's total ETH balance increases by exactly v, then the per-address balances[A] increases by exactly v (i.e., recorded per-address balance change equals the observable contract balance change for that depositor); the mutant that double-increments balances can make balances[A] increase by 2*v even though contract balance only increased by v, breaking the rule.

After any Deposit call by any actor, the caller's recorded balance in the reference contract is at least the sum of its previous recorded balance and the deposited value (no reentrancy can observe an old balance during Deposit); moving the balance update after the external Log call permits a reentrant attacker to observe and exploit the old balance so this monotonicity can be violated for some inputs.

For every deposit call by any caller, the contract's recorded balances for all addresses never decreases as a result of that single Deposit (i.e., after Deposit completes, for every address k: balances(k) >= balances_before(k)); the buggy mutant moves the balance update after an external log call allowing a reentrant attacker to cause some address's recorded balance to be lower after Deposit completes.

In the reference, for any Deposit call, after it completes the depositor's recorded balance equals previous balance plus msg.value (i.e., balances(depositor) == prev + value); the mutant that calls external Log before updating balances allows a reentrant attacker to withdraw during Deposit causing the depositor's final recorded balance to be less than prev+value for some inputs, violating this equality.

For any Deposit call by a depositor, the reference contract ensures that no other address's recorded balance decreases as a result of that Deposit; the mutant (which calls the external log before updating balances) can be re-entered by an attacker and cause some other address's recorded balance to be lower after Deposit completes.

For any Deposit invoked by an arbitrary caller, if some other address is able to re-enter and call Collect during that Deposit, the reference C ensures that after Deposit completes the reentrant caller cannot have withdrawn more than their balance allowed before the Deposit (i.e., Collect during Deposit will fail or not reduce the final balances compared to pre-Deposit), while the mutant that logs before updating balances allows a reentrant attacker to successfully Collect during Deposit and reduce balances, breaking this invariant.

For any caller and value, calling SetMinSum on the correct contract always succeeds (does not revert) when the contract has not been initialized and sets MinSum to the provided value; the mutant changes the revert semantics to require(!intitalized) which can make the call revert differently in some contexts affecting success detection — thus there exist inputs where the mutant's behavior differs (specifically a revert vs success observable via try/catch).

For any caller and uint value, calling SetMinSum on an uninitialized contract succeeds (does not revert) and sets MinSum to that value; the mutant can revert in contexts where require() consumes the call differently, causing the call to fail (observed via try/catch) while the reference succeeds.

For any caller and uint input when the contract has not been initialized, calling SetMinSum succeeds (does not revert) and sets MinSum to the provided value; the mutant can cause SetMinSum to revert (observable via try/catch) for some inputs due to changing the revert site to require(!intitalized).

For any caller and any uint _val, calling SetMinSum on an uninitialized contract always returns successfully (does not revert) and leaves a successful call observable via try/catch; the mutant turns the pre-check into require(!intitalized) which can cause a revert observable by try/catch for some inputs/contexts, so the reference always yields ok==true while the mutant can yield ok==false for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any uint _val when the contract has NOT been initialized, calling SetMinSum never reverts on the reference and thus returns success (try/catch ok==true); the mutant's use of require(!intitalized) can make the call revert in some execution contexts, causing ok==false for some fuzzed inputs.

For any caller and any uint _val, calling SetMinSum(_val) on the reference always sets MinSum equal to _val (even repeatedly before initialization), whereas the mutant leaves MinSum unchanged when intitalized==true and thus can produce a different MinSum for some inputs (caller sequence/values).

For any caller and value _val, calling SetMinSum(_val) on the correct contract always sets MinSum to _val (and does not revert unless already initialized); the mutant that sets intitalized = true before assigning MinSum can cause MinSum to remain its previous value or the call to revert differently for some inputs (due to interleaving/side-effects), so there exist inputs where MinSum differs after the call.

For any caller and value _val, calling SetMinSum(_val) on the correct contract always succeeds (does not revert) and leaves MinSum equal to _val when the contract was not yet initialized; the mutant that sets intitalized = true before assigning MinSum can cause a different observable outcome (MinSum != _val) when an adversarial reentrant caller observes intitalized==true during the call and triggers behavior that prevents MinSum from being set, so there exist inputs (a reentrant helper caller address) that make the mutant differ.

For any caller and any uint _val, calling SetMinSum(_val) on a fresh C always results in MinSum == _val after the call; the mutant can be distinguished because if SetMinSum sets intitalized = true before assigning MinSum, a reentrant helper triggered (by having SetLogFile point to a helper whose setter reacts when intitalized flips) can block or change MinSum, causing MinSum != _val for some fuzzed _val/actor.

For any caller and any uint _val, calling SetMinSum(_val) on a fresh, uninitialized C always sets MinSum to _val (call succeeds and MinSum()==_val); the mutant that sets intitalized = true before assigning MinSum can be observed to violate this for some inputs when SetLogFile points to a helper that reverts on AddMessage, causing the mutant's attempt to notify/log (triggered via deposit-like paths invoked by a malicious log) to change the outcome so MinSum != _val.

For any caller and uint _val on a fresh C, calling SetMinSum(_val) always returns ok=true (does not revert) and leaves MinSum equal to _val; the mutant that sets intitalized=true before assigning MinSum enables a reentrant attacker (deployed helper) to observe intitalized==true and reenter/modify state so that the call either reverts or MinSum != _val for some fuzzed inputs.

Rule: Once Initialized() has been called, SetLogFile must revert (cannot change Log); the mutant removes this guard so after Initialized() the reference always prevents changing Log but the mutant allows changing it for some inputs.

For any caller and any address argument, after calling SetLogFile on the correct contract the public Log getter returns the provided address cast to LogFile, whereas the mutant sets Log to the zero address so the returned Log address equals address(0) for some inputs — therefore the rule: calling SetLogFile(x) results in Log == x; the mutant violates this for inputs where x != address(0).
